newsitem.title: USA: IMF sees problems with India, Indonesia banks.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees problems with India, Indonesia banks.

text.p: India's hopes of resolving bad loan problems at its banks over the next two or three years are probably too optimistic, an International Monetary Fund report said on Wednesday.
"It is likely that the ultimate resolution of the problem will extend beyond this horizon," the annual report on international capital markets said.

While most banks' non-performing loans are believed to be manageable, four state banks are in need of assistance, the report said. "Asset quality remains a key source of concern with the Indian banking system," it added.
Turning to Indonesia, the IMF report said the country has made significant improvements in its banking system recently, including stepped-up supervision and regulation.
"Nevertheless, deficiencies in the mechanisms for enforcing loan contracts and for liquidating banks have allowed several insolvent banks to remain in place," it said.
"Some banks appear to have remained vulnerable to macroeconomic imbalances and disturbances, including increases in domestic interest rates and reversals of capital inflows," the report added.
